products.name: fixtern
products.line: Drop the files, say as little as you like, and get back what a consultant would produce, every figure naming the rows it came from.
products.title: fixtern, an AI consulting engine with every figure sourced

products.name: Favent
products.line: After an event, each guest finds every photo they appear in by showing the app their face; it is measured on their own phone or laptop and never uploaded.
products.title: Favent, find your event photos by face, on your own device

products.name: Oculane
products.line: Watches a game's economy of coins and rewards, proposes one small fix when players start to drift away, and changes nothing until a person approves it by name.
products.title: Oculane, a game economy console with human approval

products.name: Stamphall
products.line: A checkpoint between a company's AI assistants and its systems: every action an assistant asks for is checked at six windows first, and one no stops it.
products.title: Stamphall, a gateway that checks every AI agent call

products.name: Sovela
products.line: Fall asleep to music; Sovela stops it when you drift off. Your Apple Watch notices, and Sovela pauses the music on your iPhone and dims your lights.
products.title: Sovela, the sleep app that stops your music

products.name: Manita
products.line: Your own AI on your Mac: chat, a coding agent, pictures, voice, music and video, and search through your files, with every model running on the machine itself.
products.title: Manita, a local AI app for the Mac

projects.name: chess-glasses
projects.line: A chess coach in your glasses: it watches the board through the camera and says the best move in your ear.

projects.name: destroy-guard
projects.line: Stops an AI assistant from wiping out your work: before it may run a delete-everything command, a checked backup of exactly that thing has to exist.

projects.name: credential-reach
projects.line: Shows which of your passwords, keys and logins an AI assistant on your computer could get its hands on, without ever revealing them.

projects.name: pkg-vitals
projects.line: AI assistants sometimes invent software names, and attackers register them. This checks every package before the assistant installs it.

projects.name: mcp-upkeep
projects.line: Before you plug a new add-on into an AI assistant, checks whether anyone still looks after it, whether its licence allows use and whether it was withdrawn.

projects.name: agent-vitals
projects.line: A dataset published every day: it counts the AI agent repositories on GitHub and measures how many are still maintained and how many have a usable licence.

projects.name: awesome-vitals
projects.line: A tool you run on any list of links, such as a README: it finds which of the linked repositories are dead, abandoned, renamed or unlicensed, and on which line.

projects.name: Agent and skill packs
projects.line: Eleven ready-made sets of instructions that turn Claude into a specialist for spreadsheet audits, research, presentations, websites, risk and writing.

projects.name: csrd-scope
projects.line: Tells a company whether the EU's sustainability reporting law applies to it and from which year, and cites the article that says so.

projects.name: cbam-mcp
projects.line: Tells an importer whether the EU's new carbon charge at the border applies to a product, and how much CO2 the EU assumes it carries from each country.

projects.name: financed-emissions
projects.line: Shows a bank how much of its borrowers' CO2 counts as its own, from its list of loans and investments, with every step of the arithmetic visible.

projects.name: eudr-scope-mcp
projects.line: Says whether a product such as wood, cocoa or coffee falls under the EU's anti-deforestation law, from which date, and how risky its country of origin is rated.

projects.name: vsme-kit
projects.line: Helps a small firm with the EU's voluntary sustainability report: what it asks for, and a check of the filled-in form for gaps and totals that do not add up.

projects.name: eu-taxonomy-mcp
projects.line: Says which business activities count as green under EU rules for a given industry, and quotes the test each one has to pass.

projects.name: eu-ets-mcp
projects.line: Looks up how much CO2 every factory and power plant in the EU reported, and how many free pollution permits it received.

projects.name: esg-toolkit
projects.line: Four calculators: why a company's emissions moved, how fast they must fall to meet a target, which cuts are cheapest, and the carbon in imported steel.

projects.name: xlsx-review
projects.line: Shows what changed between two versions of an Excel file, formula by formula, and flags the edits that usually break a spreadsheet.

projects.name: analyst-toolkit
projects.line: Estimates the size of a market in two independent ways and shows which assumptions would have to change for them to agree; it also values a business from its expected cash.

projects.name: unitguard
projects.line: Stops a model from adding numbers whose units do not match, such as kilowatt-hours and tonnes, before they give a wrong answer that looks right.

projects.name: open-climate-data
projects.line: Labels every number with where it came from and when, and converts energy and mass units while refusing any conversion that would need a guess.

line.de: 68 Leute in Sechsergruppen brauchen 159 Treffen, eines weniger als die gelisteten 160, und weniger geht nicht; 37 Fälle sind verbessert, vier davon jetzt exakt gelöst.
